newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Dar es Salaam votes in test of opposition power.
newsitem.headline: Dar es Salaam votes in test of opposition power.

text.p: Tanzanians voted in a Dar es Salaam parliamentary by-election on Sunday in a key test pitting opposition leader Augustine Mrema against a ruling party civil servant.

Mrema, an anti-corruption campaigner, stood against Abdul Cisco Mtire of the ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi (CCM-Party for the Revolution) for Temeke seat, vacant since CCM parliamentarian Ramadhani Kihiyo resigned due to poor health three months ago.
Mtire, a little-known civil servant, received backing from President Benjamin Mkapa, cabinet ministers and other political heavyweights in more than two months of campaigning for Sunday's poll.
But most analysts expected it to be a hotly-contested race against Mrema, a former interior minister and deputy prime minister who heads the main NCCR-Mageuzi opposition party.
CCM officials said Mrema was a strong candidate so it would be a large credit for the ruling party if he was knocked out.

CCM has 217 seats and opposition parties have 54 seats in the 275-member parliament. Mrema was the main opposition candidate against Mkapa in a presidential election last year and took 27.8 percent of votes against the victor's 61.8 percent.
The National Electoral Commission said it expected to announce the result of the by-election on Monday. There are a total of 431 polling stations and 97,400 registered voters.
